cause_quote: The original probe used `!process.versions.bun&&(!requiredFlag||process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags.has(requiredFlag))?process.execPath:""`, so with no required flag it accepted the first real Node executable regardless of version.
user_saw: With OpenClaw running under Bun and Node 20 first on PATH, a Node helper could exit with a syntax error even when a supported Node was also installed.
summary: The fix applies OpenClaw’s Node version check both when reusing the current executable and when probing candidates for helper processes.
reasoning: OpenClaw already excluded Node 20 when #145688 introduced the shared resolver, but the resolver immediately served an existing subprocess launcher without checking the version floor. I checked that the later standalone probe retained the same acceptance rule and that the reported Gateway CI reproduction exercised it by placing Node 20 ahead of supported Node 24.
